summary: Give every organization a curated catalogue of request topics and make the topic the only classifier a caller supplies. One new table (RequestTopic) plus two nullable columns on Request (topicId, topicLabel) in one additive migration that also seeds the eleven default topics for every organization that already exists; the signup transaction seeds new ones. A new topics module in apps/api/src/request-topics/ answers five routes behind SessionGuard + OrgScopeGuard with create, rename, reorder, archive and restore, all scoped by session.organizationId and all status writes taken under a FOR UPDATE row lock. POST .../requests stops accepting type and accessKind (400), requires topicId, derives Request.type from the topic, snapshots the topic name into topicLabel in the creating transaction, and refuses a client-audience topic for a member addressee; GET .../requests gains a topicId filter and a status=closed value spanning declined and cancelled. packages/validation gains REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES, four REQUEST_MESSAGES keys, the topic validators, the sort comparator, the status-filter expander, one status label map read by the list, the detail header and the filter control, and manage-request-topics / ManageRequestTopics in both capability unions. The web app gains a Settings > Request topics screen and its sidebar row, loses the Type and Access kind controls from the new-request modal in favour of an About picker with an empty state, and reads its status words from the shared map. NOTE: this plan is written for a refine probe and is not executable as it stands - two findings below block it.

One exported status label map for REQ-02-028 with an entry for every member of REQUEST_STATUSES (index-typed against RequestStatus so a sixth status fails compilation) plus the closure sub-label for declined and cancelled. Add 'closed' to REQUEST_STATUS_QUERIES and an expander that maps it to ['declined','cancelled'] while every stored value still expands to itself and an unknown value still returns null (never a default) - parseRequestStatusQuery at requests.ts:456 is the function to widen, not replace. vacationStatusesFor (requests.ts:479) gains its 'closed' arm returning ['rejected','cancelled'] (TC-02-INT-17). Add topicId to IMMUTABLE_REQUEST_FIELDS (requests.ts:352) for REQ-02-024. Register the capability in BOTH unions as organization/01 established: 'manage-request-topics' in MemberCapability (index.ts:506) with a row in all four CAPABILITY_MATRIX role objects (index.ts:613), and 'ManageRequestTopics' in Capability (roles.ts:51) with entries in ROLE_CAPABILITIES.admin and .manager (roles.ts:108) - admin and manager true, user and viewer false. Every capability check reads normalizeRole() (roles.ts:37) so the legacy 'member' column value maps to user. Retire the create-body kind rules: validateNewRequest (requests.ts:294) stops calling validateRequestKind and instead rejects a body carrying type or accessKind with REQUEST_MESSAGES.classifierNotAccepted (REQ-02-022) and requires topicId with REQUEST_MESSAGES.topicRequired (REQ-02-018, including null and empty string). validateRequestKind itself stays exported - spec 01's PATCH immutability list and its unit cases still name it.

tasks.title: Schema and the one migration: RequestTopic, Request.topicId/topicLabel, functional unique index, seed backfill

migration.note: One migration for the whole run. It creates RequestTopic, adds two NULLABLE columns to Request (topicId, topicLabel VarChar(60)), creates @@index([organizationId, audience, status]) and the functional index CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "RequestTopic_organizationId_audience_name_lower_key" ON "RequestTopic" ("organizationId", "audience", LOWER("name")) - the device apps/api/prisma/migrations/20260901120000_spec_org_01_clients/migration.sql:30 already uses for Client, because Prisma's @@unique is case-sensitive. It then INSERTs the eleven seeded rows for every existing Organization with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a re-run writes nothing rather than raising. No Request row is read or written by the migration (TC-02-INT-02). No rename, no drop, no new NOT NULL on an existing table. Deploy order read from infra/deploy.sh: the migration runs as a one-off task from the NEW image at infra/deploy.sh:183-184 (via infra/migrate.sh) and the services are rolled only afterwards at infra/deploy.sh:187-188, so the new schema is live while the PREVIOUS code is still serving - an unreferenced table and two nullable columns are invisible to it.

concurrency.lock: none - the backfill is an INSERT ... SELECT over Organization inside the migration transaction

tasks.title: apps/api/src/request-topics: the catalogue module and its five routes

migration.note: no database change in this task

tasks.description: @Controller('api/organizations/:orgId') @UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard), copying apps/api/src/requests/requests.controller.ts:34. organizationId is a required argument with no default on every service method and is always req.session.organizationId - the path :orgId is checked by OrgScopeGuard (apps/api/src/auth/org-scope.guard.ts:20) and is never a selector, so a topicId from another organization answers a bare 404 on every topic route (TC-02-INT-21). The manage-request-topics check runs in the SERVICE, not through CapabilityGuard, because the spec names the exact 403 body (REQUEST_TOPIC_MESSAGES.manageForbidden) and CapabilityGuard's message is fixed at 'You do not have permission to manage templates' (apps/api/src/auth/capability.guard.ts:63 reading packages/validation/src/documents.ts:125) - the same reason HolidaysController states at apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.controller.ts:19 and RequestsController at requests.controller.ts:28. The capability is still registered in both unions by T1 and the check reads normalizeRole() through can()/hasCapability. GET accepts audience (unknown -> 400 audienceUnknown, TC-02-INT-04) and status (active default | archived | all); POST defaults sortOrder to the highest stored value in that audience plus ten; PATCH accepts name and sortOrder, accepts audience only when equal to the stored value (400 audienceImmutable) and never accepts type; archive and restore take no body. A P2002 from the functional unique index maps to 409 nameDuplicate (edge case 1), which is what makes two concurrent renames safe without a table lock. There is no DELETE handler and no service method that removes a row (REQ-02-014, TC-02-INT-20).

concurrency.lock: SELECT id, status FROM "RequestTopic" WHERE id = $1 AND "organizationId" = $2 FOR UPDATE inside the transaction, on archive, restore, rename and reorder - the shape apps/api/src/requests/requests.service.ts#lockRequest already uses for Request

tasks.title: Requests API: topic on create, snapshot, derived type, refused classifier, topicId filter, status=closed

migration.note: no database change in this task

tasks.description: createRequest (requests.service.ts:301) resolves the topic by id scoped to session.organizationId; archived, foreign or unknown all answer one 400 REQUEST_MESSAGES.topicUnavailable with an identical body (REQ-02-019, TC-02-INT-13), which is the one place this area answers 400 rather than 404 for a cross-organization id, and the Security section says so. A client-audience topic against assigneeKind 'member' answers 400 topicAudienceMismatch (REQ-02-020). type is written from the topic and topicLabel from the topic's name inside the SAME transaction as the Request insert, alongside the existing nextRequestNumber FOR UPDATE allocation - one transaction, not two. accessKind is written on no new row and keeps its stored values on old ones. listRequests (requests.service.ts:143) gains topicId (an id from another organization returns an empty array, never another organization's rows, because the filter is ANDed under scopeWhere's organizationId) and status=closed, expanded through T1's function into { status: { in: ['declined','cancelled'] } }; the five stored values stay accepted for a saved link. The counters at requests.service.ts:203 stay computed before every filter, topicId included, for the reason stated there. Both the row DTO and the detail DTO gain topic: { id, name (the SNAPSHOT topicLabel, never the catalogue's current name), audience, type, status } and null for a request raised before this spec (edge case 8). patchRequest already refuses type and accessKind through IMMUTABLE_REQUEST_FIELDS; T1 adds topicId to that list, so REQ-02-024 needs no new branch here.

FOR UPDATE on the Organization row (requests.service.ts:352); the topic is read WITHOUT a lock and re-read is not required, because a topic archived between the read and the insert only means one request was raised under a topic that had just left the picker - which edge case 2 already calls acceptable and REQ-02-010 says leaves the request untouched
